{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABWGDoPQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6Pzg_pGJ0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 41, "title": "Implement PMX sphere texture mode 3 (SubTexture) using additional UV1 in TSL", "body": "## Goal

Implement **PMX sphere texture mode 3 (`envFlag === 3`, SubTexture)** in `three-mmd-loader`'s Three.js r186 TSL / NodeMaterial pipeline. This Issue covers **mode 3 only**: do not bundle it with VMD, PMX 2.1, or other remaining features.

## Current state

- `mmd-parser@1.1.4` already provides `PmxMaterial.envFlag`, `envTextureIndex`, per-vertex `auvs`, and additional UV morphs. No parser release is expected.
- `src/loaders/MMDLoader.ts` explicitly leaves `envFlag === 3` as TODO and only loads sphere maps for modes 1 (multiply) and 2 (add).
- `src/materials/MMDToonMaterial.ts` samples the sphere map with view-based `matcapUV`, and supports add/multiply only.
- `src/materials/MMDUV.ts` exports `mmdAdditionalUV(1)`, returning the **morphed additional UV1 `vec4`** (or zero when absent). UV morphs (type 4 for additional UV1), VMD tracks, and group→UV links are already implemented in [#35](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/35).

## Implementation

1. Recognize `envFlag === 3` and valid `envTextureIndex` in the PMX material builder; load the sphere/subtexture map with its existing path/texture-handling conventions. Preserve the original flag for material diagnostics.
2. For mode 3, **sample the sphere texture using additional UV1 XY** from `mmdAdditionalUV(1).xy`, *not* the normal-dependent `matcapUV`. Use the correct PMX SubTexture **color-composition rule** after checking the specification / a trustworthy MMD implementation or reference render; do not silently treat mode 3 as mode 2 (add) or mode 1 (multiply). Document the chosen behavior.
3. Honor declared additional UV1 base values and updates from direct additional-UV1 morphs, group morphs, and named VMD tracks. Reuse the existing absolute UV evaluation and texture sampling paths rather than manually reconstructing or double-applying morph weights.
4. Preserve the existing modes 0, 1 and 2, including their UV sources, blending, sphere color morph factors (`mmdSphereColor`), transparency and shared-texture behavior. Respect sampler wrapping, transforms, texture alpha and draw/shadow behavior to the extent applicable to the mode-3 specification.
5. Handle models lacking additional UV1, invalid sphere texture index, absent/missing textures, and malformed/missing data **safely and deterministically**. Define and document the fallback for mode 3 with no declared additional UV1; avoid out-of-bounds attribute access, NaNs and shader compilation errors.
6. Use TSL only (no custom GLSL/WGSL), ensure WebGL2 via `WebGPURenderer({ forceWebGL: true })` and native WebGPU when available, and avoid unnecessary per-frame shader recompiles.
7. Keep the public MMD addon API, PMD behavior, existing MMD materials, SDEF, vertex/bone/group/material/UV morphs, shadows, outlines and the browser examples compatible.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria — automated

- [ ] A **generated PMX fixture** parsed by published `mmd-parser@1.1.4` has `envFlag === 3`, an asymmetric RGBA subtexture, and distinct asymmetric base UV0/additional UV1 XY values. Assert the parsed flags, additional UV metadata and loader material properties.
- [ ] A standalone **mode-3** material renders pixels expected from additional UV1 (and **not** ordinary UV0 or view-normal sphere UV), using independent sample-coordinate/color references; exercise different normals/camera positions to rule out accidental `matcapUV` sampling.
- [ ] Independently establish and assert the **mode-3 composition/blend rule** against the PMX/MMD reference. Assert exact RGB and alpha behavior where specified; make differences from modes 1 and 2 observable in tests.
- [ ] Direct and group-driven additional UV1 morphs, plus VMD animation/seek/reset, visibly change sampled texels as expected at weights 0, 0.5, 1 and after reset, without double application or drift.
- [ ] Missing additional UV1, missing map/invalid map index, shared textures, texture origins, repeat/clamp, material morph factors and zero/partial alpha all have safe tested behavior and do not regress existing shadow/outline paths.
- [ ] Regression tests cover sphere modes **0, 1, 2** side by side with mode 3, and models without sphere maps or extra UV channels.
- [ ] Actual TSL GPU render tests check color/alpha/depth/shadow output on **mandatory WebGL2**, plus native WebGPU when a suitable adapter is available. Compilation-only tests do not satisfy this criterion.
- [ ] Expose a generated mode-3 PMX / asymmetric checker in the existing **loopback-only private viewer** (or equivalent dev-only path) for hands-on inspection. Optional real-world PMX validation may use a model obtained directly from its creator **only after inspecting its actual mode-3 flags and README/license**. No real third-party model is necessary for CI or merging.
- [ ] Generated fixture and viewer are excluded from public example data and Pages; all real PMX/textures remain Git-ignored locally and are excluded from `npm pack`, GitHub Actions artifacts and Pages. **Do not modify existing public examples, models, motions, asset manifest, screenshots or URLs.**
- [ ] Before merge, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `MMD_EXAMPLE_FIXTURES=1 npm run build:examples`, `npm run test:examples`, and isolated JavaScript/TypeScript package consumer tests all pass.
- [ ] No licensed-model download, account login, human visual approval, npm publication or post-merge verification is required for completion.

## Required post-merge verification

**None** for Issue / PR completion. Real-model inspection remains optional and separate.

## References

- [Current PMX material loader](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/loaders/MMDLoader.ts)
- [Current TSL MMDToonMaterial](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/materials/MMDToonMaterial.ts)
- [Additional UV TSL API](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/materials/MMDUV.ts)
- [Additional UV morph documentation](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/docs/uv-morphs.md)
- [PMX sphere mode enumeration (babylon-mmd)](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/master/src/Loader/Parser/pmxObject.ts)
